briefs.learning_objective: Run one supplied stable-SDK project and verify a source change with the appropriate reload action.

required_facts.statement: Run a supplied project with `flutter run` on a physical or virtual target in debug mode to use hot reload.
After modifying a Dart source file, enter `r` in the running terminal or use the editor's hot-reload control and check the running app for the change.
Hot reload preserves application state, whereas hot restart restarts the Flutter app and loses that state.
A source change becomes visible only if the changed code executes again; use restart when the change requires application initialization to run again.

briefs.learning_objective: Declare one function's values with correct inferred types and permitted reassignment.

required_facts.statement: `var name = value;` infers the variable's type from its initializer; an explicit declaration uses `Type name = value;`.
An ordinary variable can be reassigned with `name = value;`, subject to its declared or inferred type.
`final` permits a variable to be assigned once; `const` declares a compile-time constant and is implicitly final.
Use `final` for a value that will not be reassigned and `var` for a local value that must be reassigned.

briefs.learning_objective: Correct one supplied analyzer diagnostic at its source location with clean reanalysis.

required_facts.statement: Analyzer diagnostics identify source problems with a diagnostic name, message, and source location.
Use the diagnostic's description and documented correction to edit the indicated source, then run `flutter analyze` again to check the correction.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one eligibility expression that gives the specified result for supplied inputs.

required_facts.statement: Arithmetic operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `~/`, and `%` mean addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, integer division, and remainder respectively.
Comparisons `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=` produce boolean results for equality, inequality, and ordering tests.
Combine boolean conditions using `&&` for conjunction, `||` for disjunction, and `!` for negation.
Operator precedence determines expression grouping; parentheses explicitly choose the grouping.

briefs.learning_objective: Build one interpolated label with the specified output for supplied model values.

required_facts.statement: Use single or double quotes to write a string literal.
Write `$identifier` to interpolate a variable or `${expression}` to interpolate a more complex expression in a string.
Interpolation obtains an object's string representation by calling its `toString()` method.
Use a backslash to escape a matching quote within a quoted string.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one function whose required, named and optional arguments bind as specified.

required_facts.statement: Define a function with typed parameters and a return type, using `return expression;` in its body to produce a result.
Required positional arguments bind in parameter order and must be supplied by the caller.
Parameters inside `{...}` are named and are passed with `parameterName: value`; mark a named parameter `required` when callers must provide it.
Parameters inside `[...]` are optional positional parameters; use `= constantValue` to supply a default when the caller omits an optional parameter.
An arrow body `=> expression;` is shorthand for returning that expression.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one application model whose constructor establishes all required fields.

required_facts.statement: Declare an instance's typed fields inside a class and access an instance member with `instance.member`.
A generative constructor has the class's name and initializes a newly created instance.
Use initializing formal parameters such as `ClassName(this.field);` or `ClassName({required this.field});` to assign arguments to instance fields.
Initialize final instance fields at declaration, with initializing formal parameters, or in an initializer list before the constructor body runs.
A `final` instance field is assigned once and cannot subsequently be reassigned.

briefs.learning_objective: Compose one small screen whose immutable widget tree matches the supplied UI structure.

required_facts.statement: Widgets are immutable descriptions of part of a user interface, with their configuration held in final fields.
Compose a widget tree by passing another widget to a `child` argument or a list of widgets to `children`, according to the receiving widget's API.
To change a widget's configuration, create a new widget configuration rather than mutate the existing widget.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one stateless view that derives the specified output from current inputs.

required_facts.statement: A StatelessWidget describes UI using its configuration and the BuildContext passed to its build method.
Implement `Widget build(BuildContext context)` to return the widget subtree derived from those inputs.
The framework may call build after insertion, a configuration change, or a change to an inherited dependency; do not rely on build running only once.
The build method should have no side effects beyond building a widget.

briefs.learning_objective: Repair one bounded overflow by tracing parent constraints and child size.

required_facts.statement: A parent passes constraints down, children pass chosen sizes up, and parents position their children.
Constraints specify minimum and maximum width and height, and a child chooses a size within those limits.
For an overflow, inspect the parent's constraints and the child's requested size to identify which dimension cannot fit.

Bound a child with `ConstrainedBox(constraints: const BoxConstraints(minWidth: 70, minHeight: 70, maxWidth: 150, maxHeight: 150), child: child)`; these are additional bounds within the parent constraints, not replacements for them: with a parent permitting that range an oversized child is limited to 150, but tight parent constraints can force a size outside the requested range.

briefs.learning_objective: Compose one screen section with the specified main-axis and cross-axis placement.

required_facts.statement: Row arranges its children horizontally; Column arranges its children vertically.
Set `mainAxisAlignment` to position children along the primary axis and `crossAxisAlignment` along the perpendicular axis.
`start`, `end`, and `center` select alignment within an axis, while main-axis `spaceBetween`, `spaceAround`, and `spaceEvenly` distribute free space.
For a Row, horizontal start depends on text direction; for a Column, vertical start depends on vertical direction.

briefs.learning_objective: Apply one shared Material theme so the supplied components use consistent tokens.

required_facts.statement: Set `MaterialApp(theme: ThemeData(...))` to provide an application-wide Material theme.
ThemeData supplies shared values such as a color scheme and text theme used by Material components.
Read the nearest theme with `Theme.of(context)` when styling a widget with shared theme values.
A local Theme can override the theme for its descendant subtree.

briefs.learning_objective: Declare and load one supplied image using the correct bundle key.

required_facts.statement: Declare bundled asset paths under `flutter: assets:` in pubspec.yaml, preserving the required YAML indentation.
An asset's path relative to pubspec.yaml provides its logical key in the asset bundle.
Load a declared bundled image with `Image.asset('assetKey')`; the key must match the declared resource.

briefs.learning_objective: Locate the widget responsible for one supplied visual symptom using the inspector.

required_facts.statement: Open DevTools' Flutter Inspector while the application runs to inspect its live widget tree.
Enable Select Widget Mode and select the affected area in the running app to locate its widget in the tree.
Inspect the selected widget's properties and layout information, and use its source link to connect the visual symptom to application code.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one input-dependent decision that selects the required branch for given inputs.

required_facts.statement: Use `if (booleanCondition) { ... }` to execute a block when its condition is true.
Use `else` for the alternative branch and `else if` to test another condition when previous conditions were false.
A condition must have type bool; values of other types are not implicitly treated as true or false.

briefs.learning_objective: Repair one nullable-value use with an explicit guard or fallback and no unjustified non-null assertion.

required_facts.statement: Append `?` to a type to allow null; an ordinary non-nullable type excludes null.
Guard a local nullable variable with a null check before using it as non-null, allowing flow analysis to promote it where applicable.
Use `value ?? fallback` to substitute a fallback when the value is null.
Use `?.` to access a member only when the receiver is not null.
The postfix `!` asserts that a value is not null; if it is null the assertion fails at runtime, so handle an uncertain nullable value with a check instead.

briefs.learning_objective: Construct and access one typed model collection while rejecting incompatible element types.

required_facts.statement: A `List<T>` is an ordered collection with elements constrained to T; create a typed literal with `<T>[...]` and access elements using zero-based indexing.
A `Set<T>` stores unique elements; create one with `<T>{...}` and add elements using `add`.
A `Map<K, V>` associates unique keys with values; create `<K, V>{key: value}`, write with `map[key] = value`, and read with `map[key]`.
A map lookup can return null when its key is absent, even when its value type is non-nullable.
Adding an incompatible type to a typed collection is an error rather than an automatic conversion to the element type.

briefs.learning_objective: Transform one supplied collection with a loop that produces the required accumulated result.

required_facts.statement: Use `for (var element in collection) { ... }` to process collection elements.
Declare an accumulator before the loop and update it in the loop body to build a result from the elements.
A conventional loop `for (initialization; condition; update) { ... }` repeats while its condition is true, performing the update after each iteration.
`break` stops a loop and `continue` skips the remainder of the current iteration.

briefs.learning_objective: Wire one callback so it uses the intended captured value when invoked.

required_facts.statement: A closure retains access to variables in the lexical scope where it was created.
Pass a function value as a callback rather than calling it immediately with parentheses.
Write an anonymous function with `(parameters) { ... }` or `(parameters) => expression` to use captured values when the callback is invoked.

briefs.learning_objective: Demonstrate when one supplied tree update reuses an element and when it replaces it.

required_facts.statement: The framework can update an existing element with a new widget when their runtimeType and key are equal.
Changing the widget type or key prevents that element from being updated with the new widget.
Different configuration values alone do not prevent reuse when type and key still match.

briefs.learning_objective: Place one State-owned resource's initialization, configuration rebinding when needed, and disposal at the correct lifecycle boundaries, not in repeated build calls.

required_facts.statement: A State instance can persist across multiple build calls and owns its state for that lifetime.
Override initState, call `super.initState()`, and initialize owner-lifetime resources there rather than repeatedly in build.
When an update changes a configuration-dependent resource, use didUpdateWidget to detach from the old resource and bind to the new one.
Override dispose to release owned resources and call `super.dispose()` when the framework permanently removes the State.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one local toggle whose next build reflects the changed value.

required_facts.statement: Change local State fields within `setState(() { ... });` so the framework schedules a build reflecting the changed state.
The setState callback runs synchronously and must not be async.
Changing a field without setState might not schedule a build and might leave the displayed UI unchanged.

briefs.learning_objective: Extract one repeated UI section with parameters that preserve its specified behavior.

required_facts.statement: Extract a repeated UI responsibility into a dedicated widget rather than a helper method that returns widgets.
Expose differing inputs as final constructor parameters and use those parameters in build to preserve the extracted section's behavior.
Pass a callback parameter for an action the extracted section delegates to its caller.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one form gate that rejects invalid input and submits valid input once.

required_facts.statement: Create a Form with a stable `GlobalKey<FormState>` and place TextFormFields inside it.
A TextFormField validator returns an error string for invalid input and null for valid input.
Call the form state's `validate()` from the submit handler; it runs field validators and returns true only if no field reports an error.
Place the submission action inside the successful-validation branch so an invalid form does not submit and one handler invocation performs one submission.

briefs.learning_objective: Repair one linear layout so remaining space is allocated to the intended flexible children.

required_facts.statement: Row and Column can allocate remaining main-axis space to flexible children using flex factors.
Wrap a child in Expanded to require it to fill its allocated space; wrap it in Flexible with the default loose fit to allow it to be smaller.
Set each child's `flex` to specify its proportion of remaining space relative to the other flexible children.
Flex allocation requires bounded space along the main axis; an unbounded main-axis constraint cannot supply a finite remaining space.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one overlay with the required stacking order and positioned bounds.

required_facts.statement: Stack places children in shared space and paints them in list order, with later children above earlier children.
Use Positioned inside Stack with `top`, `bottom`, `left`, or `right` to control a child's placement.
Specifying both opposite edges fixes a child's size on that axis; alternatively specify one edge and the corresponding width or height.
Stack uses non-positioned children to determine its size.

briefs.learning_objective: Render one dynamic collection so all content remains reachable within a bounded viewport.

required_facts.statement: A ListView scrolls a linear collection within a viewport so content beyond its visible area can be reached.
For a dynamic collection, use `ListView.builder(itemCount: ..., itemBuilder: ...)` to build children on demand by index.
Give a scrolling list a bounded viewport, using a constrained parent or Expanded within a bounded Column where appropriate.

briefs.learning_objective: Adapt one supplied screen so its layout meets requirements on both sides of a width breakpoint.

required_facts.statement: Use `LayoutBuilder(builder: (context, constraints) { ... })` when a layout decision depends on the space available to that subtree.
Use `MediaQuery.sizeOf(context)` for the app window's size rather than a local widget's available size.
Compare `constraints.maxWidth` with the required breakpoint and return the appropriate widget layout from an if/else branch.

briefs.learning_objective: Repair one screen so required content remains usable at the supplied enlarged text scale.

required_facts.statement: Flutter text widgets respect the operating system's font-size setting, which changes the space required by text.
Provide layout space for enlarged text; use `Flexible(child: Text(...))` in a bounded Row when text must fit the available width rather than overflow it.
Test the screen on a small target with the largest font setting and adjust its layout so required content remains accessible.

briefs.learning_objective: Label one supplied control so its semantics expose the intended accessible name.

required_facts.statement: Semantics annotates the widget tree with meaning used by accessibility tools.
Wrap a control with `Semantics(label: ..., child: ...)` to supply an accessible name when its visual representation is insufficient.
Inspect the resulting semantics and test with a screen reader to verify the control is identified as intended.

briefs.learning_objective: Correct one undersized control so its hit area meets the supplied mobile target requirement.

required_facts.statement: The interactive tap area needs enough space independently of the visual decoration's size.
Android recommends a minimum target of 48 by 48 dp and iOS 44 by 44 points.
Give the interactive control a sufficiently large layout area, for example with `ConstrainedBox(constraints: BoxConstraints(minWidth: requiredWidth, minHeight: requiredHeight), child: control)`.

briefs.learning_objective: Correct one reorderable list so each stateful item retains its identity after reordering.

required_facts.statement: A stable key combined with the same widget type lets the framework match an item's updated configuration to its element.
Set an item's `key: ValueKey(itemIdentity)` from a stable identity, not its current list position, so reordered stateful children can remain matched to the same items.

optional_enrichment.statement: In `ListView.builder`, supply `findChildIndexCallback` to map a child's key to its current index when ordering can change; without it the child may not map to its existing render object and state can be lost.

briefs.learning_objective: Place one state value at the smallest owner covering all required consumers.

required_facts.statement: Keep state above the widgets that need to use it in the widget tree.
For consumers in separate branches, choose a shared ancestor as the owner rather than duplicate the same state in each branch.
Pass state down as configuration and pass callbacks down for children to request changes from the owner.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one model mutation that exposes coherent state before notifying consumers.

required_facts.statement: A model can extend ChangeNotifier to expose state and notify listeners of changes.
Implement a mutation method that updates the model's fields before calling `notifyListeners()`.
Expose current model values through fields or getters so notified consumers can read the updated state.
Call notifyListeners when a model change might change its consumers' UI, not merely because a value was read.

briefs.learning_objective: Place one model above its intended consumers so lookup resolves the correct instance.

required_facts.statement: Place a provider as an ancestor of all widgets that need the provided value.
A lookup using BuildContext returns the nearest matching provider of the requested type.
Use a context below the provider for lookup; a context above it cannot resolve the value that provider exposes.
A non-nullable lookup throws when there is no matching provider.
Expose the supplied existing model with `Provider<Model>.value(value: suppliedModel, child: consumerSubtree)`, where Model is its type and consumerSubtree contains the intended consumers.

briefs.learning_objective: Invoke one model action using a provider read that does not subscribe the caller.

required_facts.statement: `context.read<T>()` retrieves the model without subscribing the calling widget to its changes.
Inside an event callback, call `context.read<Model>().action()` to invoke a model action without registering a rebuild dependency.
`Provider.of<T>(context, listen: false)` provides a non-listening lookup equivalent to read.
Do not use a non-listening read as the mechanism for a build output that must update when the model changes.

briefs.learning_objective: Connect one consumer so relevant model changes update its UI without unrelated subscriptions.

required_facts.statement: Use `context.watch<T>()` in build when the widget's output depends on changes to that model.
Use `context.select<T, R>((model) => selectedValue)` to subscribe to a selected part rather than the entire model.
Consumer provides a builder receiving the model and rebuilds that consumer when the provided model notifies.
Keep a subscription near the UI that uses its data rather than subscribing a larger unrelated subtree.

briefs.learning_objective: Correct one provider declaration so its owned model is disposed once at the correct lifetime boundary.

required_facts.statement: Use `ChangeNotifierProvider(create: (_) => Model(), child: ...)` for a newly created model that the provider owns.
ChangeNotifierProvider automatically disposes a model it creates when that provider leaves the tree.
Use `ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: existingModel, child: ...)` to expose an already-owned model rather than transfer its ownership through create.

briefs.learning_objective: Refactor one mixed handler into supplied UI, application and data layers without changing behavior.

required_facts.statement: In the recommended architecture, a view renders data and forwards interaction events rather than implement business or data-source logic.
Keep application state and action orchestration in the application layer, exposing the values and callbacks that the view needs.
Place source-specific external access in the data layer and call it through the existing layer boundary rather than put that access in the view.
Refactor an event handler to call a command while keeping its input and observable outcome unchanged, rather than make the view perform the data operation itself.

briefs.learning_objective: Build one minimal test harness providing the supplied widget's required context and dependencies.

required_facts.statement: Define a widget test using `testWidgets('description', (tester) async { ... });`, which supplies a WidgetTester.
Use `await tester.pumpWidget(widget)` to build and render the widget under test.
Include the required application ancestors, such as MaterialApp for a Material screen, in the tree passed to pumpWidget.
Provide the widget's model dependencies above it in the harness so its lookups can resolve them.

briefs.learning_objective: Assert one observable UI result with an appropriate finder and matcher in a supplied harness.

required_facts.statement: Use `find.text('text')` to locate Text widgets displaying a given string.
Use `find.byKey(key)` for a keyed widget or `find.byType(Type)` to locate widgets of a type.
Assert a finder result with `expect(finder, findsOneWidget)` for one match or `findsNothing` for no match.
Create the widget tree before evaluating a finder-based assertion.

briefs.learning_objective: Simulate one interaction and pump the test so its required visible change can be observed.

required_facts.statement: Simulate a tap using `await tester.tap(finder)` and text entry using `await tester.enterText(finder, text)`.
Use `await tester.pump()` after an interaction to process a frame before checking the changed UI.
Use `pumpAndSettle()` when a finite sequence of scheduled frames must finish, rather than assume a tap immediately rebuilds the test tree.
Assert the observable UI after pumping to verify the interaction's effect.

briefs.learning_objective: Handle one expected exception without swallowing unrelated failures.

required_facts.statement: `throw` raises an exception and execution unwinds until a matching handler is found.
Handle a known exception type with `try { ... } on ExpectedType catch (e) { ... }` rather than catch all failures indiscriminately.
Use `catch (e, stackTrace)` when the handler needs both the exception and its trace.
Use `rethrow` when a caught failure must propagate to another handler instead of be swallowed.

optional_enrichment.statement: A finally block executes for cleanup whether or not an exception was thrown.

briefs.learning_objective: Diagnose one runtime error using its first actionable application frame and framework context.

required_facts.statement: Flutter catches errors from framework callbacks and reports them through FlutterError.onError; the default handler presents them in device logs.
Read the reported exception and framework context, then inspect the call stack to locate the application call that caused the failure.
Select the first relevant application frame and inspect that frame's source and variables rather than treat a framework reporting frame as the faulty application statement.

briefs.learning_objective: Consume one Future so pending, successful and failed completion are distinguished correctly.

required_facts.statement: A Future represents an operation that is uncompleted or completed with either a value or an error.
A `Future<T>` produces a value of type T on successful completion; the Future itself is not that eventual value.
Register a success callback with `future.then(onValue, onError: onError)` to distinguish successful and failed completion.

Future completion and callback execution are distinct: when `then` is registered on an already-completed Future, its callback is scheduled in a later microtask rather than called immediately, so a callback not yet having run does not mean the Future is still uncompleted.

briefs.learning_objective: Complete one awaited submit handler so success and expected failure reach the appropriate outcome.

required_facts.statement: Declare an asynchronous function with `async` and a return type such as `Future<T>` or `Future<void>`.
Inside an async function, use `await future` to obtain its completed value before executing dependent statements.
Await suspends the asynchronous function while other asynchronous work can run; it does not synchronously block the application waiting for the result.
Wrap an awaited operation in a typed try/catch to route its expected failure to the failure outcome.

briefs.learning_objective: Import one supplied package so its required symbol resolves without a namespace error.

required_facts.statement: Import a supplied package library with `import 'package:package_name/library.dart';` so its exported names are available in the file.
Use an import prefix `as prefix` and refer to `prefix.Symbol` to disambiguate conflicting names.
Use `show` to expose selected imported names or `hide` to exclude selected names.
An SDK library uses a `dart:` URI, while a package library uses a `package:` URI.

briefs.learning_objective: Call one supplied REST endpoint with the correct request arguments and response branch.

required_facts.statement: Call `http.get(Uri.parse(endpoint), headers: headers)` for a GET request and await its Response.
Call `http.post(uri, headers: headers, body: encodedBody)` for a POST request requiring a payload; JSON payloads can be encoded with `jsonEncode` and a matching content-type header.
Inspect the response's `statusCode` and `body` and branch according to the endpoint contract rather than assume every completed HTTP request succeeded.
The fetch-data recipe accepts status 200, while the create-album recipe accepts 201; these are the recipes' endpoint contracts, not a universal single success code.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one model decode/encode mapping that preserves the specified fields and Dart types.

required_facts.statement: Decode a JSON response with `jsonDecode` and map the resulting fields into a typed model rather than pass an untyped map through the application.
Implement `Model.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json)` to read named keys and check or cast the values to the model's declared field types.
Implement `Map<String, dynamic> toJson()` to return the corresponding wire keys and field values.
Use `jsonEncode` on the model's JSON-compatible mapping, or on a model with toJson, to produce encoded JSON.
Keep decode and encode key names and field types consistent with the data contract.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one request state model with the required loading, success, empty and error transitions.

required_facts.statement: Represent pending work as loading, a successful result as data, and failed completion as error rather than report success while waiting.
Branch on completion state and error presence before reading the result; a FutureBuilder builder can distinguish waiting, an error, and completed data.
After successful completion, check a returned collection's `isEmpty` to distinguish empty results from results containing data.
Publish the corresponding single presentation state at each transition: loading when a request begins and error, empty, or non-empty success when it completes.

briefs.learning_objective: Guard one asynchronous completion so it never updates a disposed UI owner.

required_facts.statement: Calling setState after State disposal is an error.
Check `if (!mounted) return;` after awaited work and before a State update so a completion cannot update an unmounted owner.
Where possible, cancel work or detach the completion source when the owner is disposed rather than rely only on checking mounted.

briefs.learning_objective: Add a bounded timeout and explicit user retry to one supplied request.

required_facts.statement: Use `future.timeout(Duration(...))` to bound how long the returned future waits for the source future.
Without an onTimeout handler, exceeding the time limit completes the timeout future with TimeoutException.
Timeout does not cancel the original operation; it may still finish after the timeout result has been delivered.
Wire a retry action to invoke the request function again and update the displayed request state from that new attempt.

briefs.learning_objective: Prevent an older completion from overwriting the result of a newer request.

required_facts.statement: Asynchronous requests can finish in a different order from the order in which they were started.
Assign a distinct identity to a new request, store it as the current identity, and capture it in that request's completion callbacks.
Before publishing either a result or an error, compare the captured identity with the current identity and ignore a completion whose identity no longer matches.
FutureBuilder uses callback identities to ignore callbacks after replacement of its future or disposal of its State.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one supplied Flutter API contract with all required members and valid polymorphic use.

required_facts.statement: Every class implicitly defines an interface consisting of its instance members and the interfaces it implements.
Declare `class Implementation implements Contract` and provide the APIs required by Contract rather than inherit its implementation.
A caller typed as Contract can use an implementing instance through the members exposed by that contract.
Use compatible member parameter and return types so the implementation satisfies the interface.

Declare `class Subclass extends Superclass` to inherit the superclass implementation; subclasses can override instance methods, getters, and setters, marking intentional overrides with `@override`, and an overriding method must accept the same number of positional parameters, use the same or broader parameter types and the same or narrower return type, and match whether the method is generic.

briefs.learning_objective: Move one data operation behind the supplied repository contract without exposing source details to UI.

required_facts.statement: A repository provides application-facing data while hiding the service or storage details used to obtain it.
Put source access and raw-data conversion in the data layer, and expose a repository method returning the application's data contract.
Have the view model call the repository contract rather than make the UI depend on a concrete transport or storage API.

briefs.learning_objective: Make one asynchronous test assert only after controlled work completes.

required_facts.statement: Await controlled asynchronous work before asserting a result that depends on its completion.
In a widget test, pump after the work completes to render the state change before checking the UI.
`pump(duration)` advances the test clock by the requested duration and schedules a frame; `pumpAndSettle()` pumps until no frames are scheduled.
Use a finite known completion point rather than pumpAndSettle when ongoing activity continually schedules frames.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one two-screen flow with the expected push and pop destination sequence.

required_facts.statement: Navigator manages a stack of routes, with the current route at the top.
Push a new screen with `Navigator.push(context, MaterialPageRoute(builder: (context) => Destination()))`.
Return from the current route using `Navigator.pop(context)`, which removes the top route and reveals the route beneath it.

briefs.learning_objective: Pass one typed model argument so the destination receives its required input.

required_facts.statement: Declare a destination's model input as a typed final field and require it through the screen's constructor.
Construct the destination inside the route builder with `Destination(model: selectedModel)` to pass the intended model value.
Read that model field in the destination's build method to render the selected data rather than rely on unrelated global state.

briefs.learning_objective: Return one selection result and correctly handle dismissal in its awaiting caller.

required_facts.statement: Await `Navigator.push<T>(...)` in the caller to obtain the route's completion result.
Return a selection using `Navigator.pop(context, selectedValue)` in the destination.
The returned value is nullable because route dismissal can occur without a selection; branch on null before using it as a selected value.
After awaiting route completion, check owner liveness before updating its UI.

briefs.learning_objective: Configure ordinary supplied destinations so their locations resolve to the expected screens.

required_facts.statement: Create a GoRouter with a list of `GoRoute(path: ..., builder: ...)` definitions mapping locations to screen configurations.
Use `MaterialApp.router(routerConfig: router)` to connect the router configuration to the application.
Navigate to a configured location with `context.go(location)`; it replaces the stack with the screens configured for that location.

briefs.learning_objective: Validate and consume one route parameter while rejecting invalid values.

required_facts.statement: Declare a path parameter with a colon-prefixed segment such as `:parameterName`, then read it from `state.pathParameters['parameterName']`.
Read query-string values from `state.uri.queryParameters['parameterName']`.
Check that a nullable route parameter is present before converting it; for an integer contract use `int.tryParse(rawValue)` and reject a null parse result before constructing the destination.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one safe fallback for an unrecognized application location.

required_facts.statement: An unmatched or unusable location can produce a GoException rather than a valid destination.
Provide `errorBuilder: (context, state) => ErrorScreen(state.error)` to render a deliberate fallback for a routing exception.
`onException` can choose a recovery navigation and takes precedence over errorBuilder and errorPageBuilder when provided.

briefs.learning_objective: Connect one supplied external URI to its correct route on cold application entry.

required_facts.statement: A deep link conveys an external URL that must be mapped to an in-app route.
GoRouter displays the configured screen matching the URL path received from the platform.
Enable the documented Android app-link or iOS universal-link configuration and match the incoming path in the router.
Verify cold-start entry as well as running-app entry because the platform delivers initial navigation differently on Android and iOS.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one back-handling policy that preserves the supplied route and unsaved-edit requirements.

required_facts.statement: Use PopScope around a route and set `canPop` from the current back-navigation policy to allow or block route dismissal.
`onPopInvokedWithResult` reports an attempted pop, and its `didPop` value indicates whether the route actually popped.
When unsaved changes block dismissal, handle `onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, result) async { ... }`, return if didPop is true, and otherwise obtain confirmation before performing an allowed pop.

On iOS with CupertinoRouteTransitionMixin, `canPop: false` prevents gesture detection and its callback is not invoked for that gesture; Android reports a blocked system-back attempt with didPop false.

briefs.learning_objective: Execute one supplied device journey and verify its observable acceptance result.

required_facts.statement: Use the integration_test package to exercise collaborating application components in a target runtime.
Initialize the test binding with `IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` and start the app from a test under integration_test.
Run the integration test on the selected device with `flutter test integration_test`.
Use tester interactions, pump as required, and assert the journey's observable acceptance result rather than only that the app launched.

briefs.learning_objective: Select one maintained package that meets supplied capability and platform requirements.

required_facts.statement: Check a candidate package's documented capability and supported platforms against the needed feature and targets.
Evaluate the package's completeness, documentation and API usability, publisher, license, and quality score; a Flutter Favorite designation is not a guarantee of suitability.
Check that the package's SDK and platform requirements are compatible with the application before adopting it.

briefs.learning_objective: Resolve one ordinary dependency conflict with compatible constraints and a reproducible lockfile.

required_facts.statement: Dependency constraints specify the allowed versions from which pub must resolve a mutually compatible dependency graph.
Caret syntax permits compatible versions up to the next breaking-version boundary, rather than pinning one exact version.
Adjust incompatible constraints to a mutually supported range, then run `flutter pub get` to resolve dependencies.
The application's pubspec.lock records the resolved versions; retain it to make application dependency resolution reproducible.
Forcing an unsupported version through dependency_overrides can break the application and is not proof of compatibility.

briefs.learning_objective: Configure one supplied plugin on Android and iOS using its documented platform setup.

required_facts.statement: A plugin's Dart dependency alone may not complete its platform setup; follow its documented Android and iOS installation requirements.
Check the plugin's required Flutter, Android, and Xcode versions and integration mode against the project configuration.

For permission_handler, AndroidX support and the documented compile SDK are platform setup requirements; on iOS, follow the instructions for the project's Swift Package Manager or CocoaPods integration.
Build and run on each required platform after applying its setup to verify the integration.

briefs.learning_objective: Add the documented Android and iOS declarations required by one supplied plugin.

required_facts.statement: Android capability permissions required by permission_handler are added to AndroidManifest.xml; the main manifest generally covers application builds.
On iOS, add the capability's corresponding usage-description key and explanation in Info.plist.
Use the plugin's permission-to-key table and platform-specific setup rather than add every possible capability declaration.
These declarations describe capability use but do not replace the user's runtime authorization decision.

briefs.learning_objective: Request one capability permission at its supplied feature's point of need.

required_facts.statement: Read a capability's current status with `await Permission.capability.status`.
Call `await Permission.capability.request()` when the feature needs authorization and use the returned status to decide whether to proceed.
A request returns the new permission status; if permission was already granted, requesting it again does not display another authorization dialog.
Limit permission requests to access relevant to the requested feature and respect the user's decision.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one denial fallback that distinguishes recoverable denial from restricted access without repeated prompting.

required_facts.statement: A denied status can mean permission was not requested or was denied before; restricted means the operating system limits access, such as through parental controls.
A permanentlyDenied request result means the user must change permission in system settings rather than receive another prompt.
Branch on the request result and provide an unavailable-feature fallback for denied or restricted access rather than continue as if access were granted.
Offer `openAppSettings()` for an appropriate permanently denied case instead of repeatedly presenting a permission prompt.
On Android, the status getter reports denied even for permanent denial, so use the request result when distinguishing permanent denial.

briefs.learning_objective: Add one fallback that works when a supplied device capability is unsupported or unavailable.

required_facts.statement: Device and platform capabilities are conditional; the application should not assume the same features are available on all targets.
Use a capability check or the adapter's availability result and select an alternative behavior when the capability is absent rather than invoke it unconditionally.
For a permission-backed service, authorization and service availability are separate checks; permission_handler exposes `serviceStatus.isEnabled` for supported services.

briefs.learning_objective: Map one supplied method contract to matching Dart names and codec-compatible arguments.

required_facts.statement: A method channel connects Dart and platform participants using an agreed channel name and method names.
Construct `MethodChannel(channelName)` with the handler's channel name and pass the agreed method name to invokeMethod.
Use arguments supported by the channel's codec; the standard codec supports values including booleans, numbers, strings, typed data, lists, maps, and null.
Channel payloads are serialized across the boundary rather than carry arbitrary Dart application objects directly.

briefs.learning_objective: Invoke one supplied native handler from Dart and decode its expected result without writing native code.

required_facts.statement: Invoke a provided platform method with `await channel.invokeMethod<T>(methodName, arguments)`.
The returned Future completes with a result that can be null, so validate nullability and the expected result type before using it.
The generic T must match the returned value's runtime type or a runtime TypeError can occur.
Decode nested list or map results according to the method contract rather than assume a deeply typed generic container is inferred automatically.

briefs.learning_objective: Handle one channel call's platform error and missing-handler outcomes distinctly.

required_facts.statement: A platform plugin failure completes invokeMethod with PlatformException; an unimplemented method completes it with MissingPluginException.
Wrap the awaited invocation in typed handlers for PlatformException and MissingPluginException to give those outcomes distinct recovery behavior.

briefs.learning_objective: Select and justify one storage mechanism for the supplied durability and access requirements.

required_facts.statement: Key-value preferences fit small, simple non-critical settings and support int, double, bool, String, and List<String>.
An application file fits data that the application reads and writes as file contents.
SQLite is a local database suitable for large amounts of structured local data, rather than a few simple settings or a file of application-managed contents.
Choose the mechanism according to the data shape and retrieval operations; preferences are not suitable for critical data because durable persistence is not guaranteed when a write returns.

briefs.learning_objective: Persist and reload one ordinary preference with its intended key and supported value type.

required_facts.statement: Use a preference key consistently with its typed setter and getter, such as `setBool(key, value)` and `getBool(key)`.
Await an asynchronous setter before continuing with code that depends on the operation's completion.
A missing preference can produce null; use a null check or `?? defaultValue` to supply the intended default.
Use `remove(key)` when the stored setting should return to its absent/default state.

briefs.learning_objective: Write and read one app-owned file using supplied directory resolution and awaited completion.

required_facts.statement: Obtain an application documents directory with `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` and construct a File using that directory's path and the intended filename.
Use `await file.writeAsString(contents)` to save text and `await file.readAsString()` to load it.
Serialize structured content into text before writing and decode the text after reading when the file's contract is JSON.
Handle expected missing-file or invalid-content failures according to the application's default/recovery contract rather than assume a saved file always exists and decodes successfully.

briefs.learning_objective: Persist and retrieve one sensitive value through supplied secure-storage APIs rather than preferences.

required_facts.statement: FlutterSecureStorage stores sensitive key-value data using platform-specific secure storage rather than ordinary preferences.
Create a FlutterSecureStorage instance and write a secret with `await storage.write(key: key, value: secret)`.
Read with `await storage.read(key: key)` and handle the nullable result when no value is available.
Remove an obsolete secret with `await storage.delete(key: key)`.
Apply the target platform's documented setup and accessibility configuration so stored data has the required availability and protection.

briefs.learning_objective: Open one supplied embedded database with the expected initial tables and fields.

required_facts.statement: A SQLite schema defines named tables, their columns, column types, and record identity constraints.

Open the supplied database with `await openDatabase(path, version: 1, onCreate: (db, version) async { await db.execute('CREATE TABLE tableName (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, fieldName TEXT)'); })`: path identifies the database file, 1 is the initial schema version, and onCreate is the creation callback that creates its tables; substitute the supplied schema's table names, column names, and column types.
Use an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY for an integer row identity and map the model's fields to matching column names.
SQLite storage types supported by sqflite include numeric values, String, Uint8List, and null; encode a bool as 0/1 rather than store a Dart bool directly.

briefs.learning_objective: Insert one record through the supplied adapter and verify its stored fields and generated identity.

required_facts.statement: Convert a model to a map whose keys match the table's columns and whose values use supported storage types.
Insert it with `await db.insert(tableName, modelMap)`.
The insert helper returns the inserted row's integer id on a successful ordinary insert; store or return that id when later operations need the record's identity.
Await the insert's completion rather than report a durable record was created before the operation succeeds.

briefs.learning_objective: Load one filtered record list through the supplied adapter and map the expected typed result.

required_facts.statement: Use `await db.query(tableName, columns: selectedColumns, where: 'id = ?', whereArgs: [id])` to read records matching an identity.
A query returns a list of row maps; check whether the list is empty before accessing a first row.
Convert a result map into the application model using its column names and declared field types.
Pass values through whereArgs rather than interpolate them into SQL predicates.

briefs.learning_objective: Update one selected record's field through the supplied adapter while preserving identity and unrelated data.

required_facts.statement: Update matching rows with `await db.update(tableName, valuesMap, where: 'id = ?', whereArgs: [id])`; include the fields to change in valuesMap.
Use a predicate identifying the intended record so the mutation does not affect unrelated rows.
The update helper returns the affected-row count; use it to distinguish a successful match from a missing record.
Re-read the record when verification requires proving that the persisted fields changed and unrelated fields stayed unchanged.

briefs.learning_objective: Delete one selected record through the supplied adapter without removing unrelated records.

required_facts.statement: Delete a selected record using `await db.delete(tableName, where: 'id = ?', whereArgs: [id])`.
Keep the identity predicate in the delete operation so only the intended record is removed.
Use the returned affected-row count to determine whether a row matched the deletion.
A subsequent query for the deleted identity should return no row while queries for other identities still return their records.

briefs.learning_objective: Apply one additive version migration while preserving the existing fixture data.

required_facts.statement: Increment openDatabase's version when changing the database schema; onCreate only handles a database that does not yet exist.
Use `onUpgrade(db, oldVersion, newVersion)` to migrate an existing database and guard each migration step with its old-version condition.
An additive column change can use `ALTER TABLE tableName ADD columnName columnType` to retain the existing table and records.
Update onCreate to create the latest schema for fresh installations as well as add the upgrade path for existing installations.
Verify the upgraded database by reading records created under the old schema; recreating a database from scratch does not test preservation.

briefs.learning_objective: Handle one failed write without falsely reporting committed durable state.

required_facts.statement: Await each persistence operation and report success only after it completes successfully.
An exception thrown out of a transaction causes rollback; completing its callback without an exception commits the transaction.
Do not suppress a persistence exception inside the transaction when rollback is required; propagate it to the boundary that translates failure for the caller.
Use the transaction object for operations inside `db.transaction((txn) async { ... })`, rather than call the database object and deadlock.
Catch expected SQL failures with `on DatabaseException catch (e)` at the persistence boundary and return or propagate the application-facing failure rather than report success.

briefs.learning_objective: Consume one event stream and cancel its subscription when its owner is disposed.

required_facts.statement: Use `stream.listen(onData, onError: onError, onDone: onDone)` to receive repeated data, error, and completion events.
The listen call returns a StreamSubscription that represents the listener's ownership of the subscription.
Store the subscription and cancel it when its owner no longer needs updates; a canceled listener stops receiving events.
If a State-owned source changes, cancel the old subscription before listening to the replacement and cancel the remaining subscription in dispose.

briefs.learning_objective: Correct one supplied access decision so it relies on service enforcement rather than a bypassable client check.

required_facts.statement: Server-enforced access rules are the authority for whether a remote data operation is permitted.
A client-side validation rule or hidden UI action does not substitute for a rule that denies the operation at the remote data boundary.
An allow-all test configuration permits anyone to read and overwrite data, so remove it and enforce the intended access policy before production use.
Keep client checks for user feedback, but require the backend policy to protect the same operation even if those checks are bypassed.

briefs.learning_objective: Initialize one supplied FlutterFire configuration before invoking its service client.

required_facts.statement: Use the target-appropriate Firebase options supplied by the generated firebase_options.dart configuration.
Import firebase_core and the generated options file, then call `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` before asynchronous Firebase initialization.
Await `Firebase.initializeApp(options: DefaultFirebaseOptions.currentPlatform)` before starting application code that uses Firebase services.
Rebuild and run the application after applying configuration so the target's platform integration is included.

briefs.learning_objective: Wire one sign-in/sign-out flow with the correct session outcome and recoverable failure behavior.

required_facts.statement: Await `FirebaseAuth.instance.signInWithEmailAndPassword(email: email, password: password)` when email/password is the enabled sign-in provider.
The sign-in Future supplies UserCredential on success; use successful completion rather than a button tap as the sign-in outcome.
Handle FirebaseAuthException and its code to translate expected authentication failures into an application-facing error.
Sign out with `await FirebaseAuth.instance.signOut()` and let the authentication-state owner reflect the result.

briefs.learning_objective: Observe one supplied session stream so UI reacts to sign-in and sign-out changes.

required_facts.statement: Subscribe to `FirebaseAuth.instance.authStateChanges()` to receive the current sign-in state and subsequent sign-in or sign-out changes.
The listener receives User?; null means signed out and a User means signed in.
The stream emits an initial event after subscription, so initialize the application's session view from that event rather than presume a stored session exists.
Cancel the owned subscription when its session-state owner ends.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one route guard that selects the allowed destination from session state.

required_facts.statement: A router redirect callback can inspect application session state and return a permitted location when the requested route requires sign-in.
Return null, or the original path, when the intended route is permitted so navigation continues without another redirect.
Keep the sign-in location allowed while signed out, rather than redirect that location back to itself in a loop.
Use routing for presentation but retain backend authorization for protected data; an app-side route gate is not the security boundary.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one document-backed edit that reads and writes the intended path and payload.

required_facts.statement: Address the intended document with `db.collection(collectionPath).doc(documentId)`; keep that reference for both the read and the write.
Await `reference.get()` to obtain a DocumentSnapshot and check for an absent document or absent data before mapping its fields into the edit model.
Write the contract's field mapping with `await reference.set(payloadMap)`; an ordinary set creates or overwrites the addressed document.
For a partial edit that must preserve unspecified fields, use `reference.set(payloadMap, SetOptions(merge: true))` rather than overwrite the whole document.
Await write completion before reporting success and keep the selected path and encoded field names consistent between the read and edited payload.

briefs.learning_objective: Handle one denied service operation under supplied rules without broadening authorization.

required_facts.statement: Cloud Firestore Security Rules evaluate mobile and web client requests and deny an operation when its access conditions are not satisfied.
Catch an expected Firebase failure around the awaited operation with `on FirebaseException catch (e)` and inspect its code to distinguish the documented denied-access outcome.
Translate a denied operation into an application-facing access failure rather than treat it as successful data retrieval or mutation.
Do not recover by making the rules allow all access: handle the denied operation under the existing policy and obtain authorized access only through the policy's permitted conditions.

briefs.learning_objective: Implement one supplied retention policy so account changes delete only the appropriate local data.

required_facts.statement: Observe account transitions from the session stream and apply the retention policy to the previous owner's local data rather than assume a new account owns it.
Identify the local keys or records assigned to the departing account and separately identify device-wide or other-owner data that the retention policy preserves.
Remove selected preference or secure-storage keys with `remove(key)` or `delete(key: key)`, rather than clear an entire store containing data that must be retained.
For database-backed account data, pass the ownership predicate and bound arguments to `db.delete(tableName, where: ownershipPredicate, whereArgs: ownerValues)` so unrelated records remain.
Await the policy-directed deletions and verify that the departing account's selected data is absent while retained data remains.

briefs.learning_objective: Handle one foreground message with the specified in-app response using supplied messaging setup.

required_facts.statement: Subscribe to `FirebaseMessaging.onMessage.listen((RemoteMessage message) { ... })` for messages received while the app is in the foreground.
Read RemoteMessage.data for the application payload and RemoteMessage.notification for any notification metadata, according to the message contract.
Foreground notification messages do not display a visible notification by default on Android or iOS; handle receipt with the specified in-app response instead of assume the system displayed it.
Cancel the owned onMessage subscription when the response owner is disposed.

briefs.learning_objective: Connect one validated notification-open payload to the expected existing route.

required_facts.statement: For a notification that opens a terminated app, await `FirebaseMessaging.instance.getInitialMessage()` and handle its nullable RemoteMessage.
For a notification that opens an app from the background, subscribe to `FirebaseMessaging.onMessageOpenedApp`.
Extract destination data from RemoteMessage.data, validate it using the destination's route contract, and then navigate to the intended screen.
Handle both entry paths because foreground message receipt via onMessage is not itself the notification-open interaction.

briefs.learning_objective: Record one non-sensitive event only under the supplied consent and privacy controls.

required_facts.statement: Emit a custom analytics event with `await FirebaseAnalytics.instance.logEvent(name: eventName, parameters: parameterMap)`.
Event names are case-sensitive; use the same name and prescribed parameter names for repeated occurrences of an interaction.
Custom parameter names must start with a letter, contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores, and be at most 40 characters; supported parameter values include String and num.

When consent is required, keep analytics collection disabled until it is granted and use `setAnalyticsCollectionEnabled(false)` or `setAnalyticsCollectionEnabled(true)` to control collection as that state changes.
Use only the event contract's necessary non-sensitive fields rather than pass entire user or application objects as telemetry.
Check the consent control before invoking logEvent and pass only the consent-approved non-sensitive fields; disabling collection is not a reason to construct an unnecessary personal-data payload.

briefs.learning_objective: Investigate one supplied slow screen in profile mode and identify its common frame bottleneck from evidence.

required_facts.statement: Measure Flutter performance in profile mode on a representative physical device rather than use debug-mode timing as production performance evidence.
Run the application with `flutter run --profile`, open the DevTools Performance view, and record the target interaction.
Each frame includes UI-thread work that builds the layer tree and raster-thread work that rasterizes it.
At 60 Hz, a frame taking more than roughly 16 ms misses the frame budget; at 120 Hz, the budget is roughly 8 ms.
In the Performance view, select a slow frame and compare its UI and raster timings to identify which stage exceeded the budget.
Use frame analysis and timeline events to identify the expensive operation before changing code.

briefs.learning_objective: Trace one unrelated subtree rebuild to its causing state dependency using supplied instrumentation.

required_facts.statement: Enable Track Widget Builds in DevTools Performance tracing to show named widget build events in the timeline.
Trigger the state change once and correlate the resulting subtree build events with the instrumented model notifications or setState call.
A setState call invalidates its State's subtree, while a provider watch subscribes its calling widget to model changes; trace which dependency or ancestor invalidation reaches the unrelated subtree.
Compare the values actually rendered by the rebuilt subtree with the changed state to identify a rebuild caused by an overly broad dependency rather than a relevant visible-data change.

briefs.learning_objective: Apply one localized rebuild fix with unchanged visible behavior and a smaller measured rebuild scope.

required_facts.statement: Localize setState to the subtree whose appearance actually changes rather than trigger rebuilding an unnecessarily large tree.
Split a large build method into widgets according to how its UI sections change.
Use const widget configurations where possible so the framework can avoid redundant rebuild work for unchanged subtrees.
With provider, use select for the specific model value needed by a consumer and use Consumer's child argument for an unchanged subtree.
Re-record the same interaction after narrowing rebuild scope to verify the change reduced measured build work.

briefs.learning_objective: Use supplied retention or subscription-count evidence across repeated route visits to identify one leaking owner and verify that a localized correction stops accumulation.

required_facts.statement: An object remains reachable, and cannot be collected, while a path of references from a root retains it.
Record the baseline retained-instance or active-subscription count, repeat route entry and exit, and compare snapshots or counts for persistent accumulation after the owner exits.
Inspect a retained instance's retaining path to find the owner or callback reference keeping it reachable.
Dispose owned disposable resources and cancel owned subscriptions when their lifetime ends, then repeat the same route visits to verify the retained resource count returns to baseline.

briefs.learning_objective: Set one application's Android and iOS identifiers to match supplied service and store registrations.

required_facts.statement: Set Android defaultConfig.applicationId to the registered application identity; after the app is uploaded to Play Store its applicationId cannot change.
When changing Android applicationId and namespace, update the MainActivity package declaration and its directory placement to match.
In Xcode, open the Runner target's General settings and set Bundle Identifier to the registered iOS App ID.
Check those identifiers against the intended service and store registrations; a user-facing display name is not the platform application identity.

briefs.learning_objective: Apply supplied release version and build values, checking Android's increasing versionCode separately from App Store version-and-build identification rules.

required_facts.statement: Declare a Flutter application version in pubspec.yaml as `version: buildName+buildNumber`; Android maps these to versionName and versionCode.
Android versionCode is a positive integer that must increase with successive releases, independently of the user-visible versionName; do not reuse a previous Play upload's versionCode.
For iOS, build-name maps to CFBundleShortVersionString and build-number to CFBundleVersion.

App Store Connect associates an uploaded build with the bundle ID and version record and uses the build string to distinguish the build; validate the version-and-build combination under Apple's upload rules rather than impose Android's globally increasing versionCode rule.
Apply the intended build values through pubspec.yaml or the `--build-name` and `--build-number` build options and verify the resulting platform values.

briefs.learning_objective: Check one release candidate against supplied dated authoritative platform requirements and identify unmet items.

required_facts.statement: Check the release against the authoritative policy effective on its intended submission date, including the target platform and whether it is a new app, update, or existing-app availability check.

Google Play target-API requirements distinguish new/update submissions from continued availability of existing apps and include platform-specific exceptions and dated deadlines; compare the candidate's target SDK with its applicable row.
Apple publishes dated SDK and toolchain submission requirements; compare the candidate's build SDK and Xcode version with the requirement effective for that upload.

A locally successful build is not evidence that store requirements are satisfied; mark each unmet candidate value against the applicable policy item rather than infer eligibility from the installed toolchain.

briefs.learning_objective: Run one build with the supplied environment variant and verify the selected inputs.

required_facts.statement: An Android product flavor represents a configured variant of the application, such as staging or production.
Use the named Android product flavor already present in the project configuration rather than substitute values from another environment.
Select a variant with `flutter run --flavor flavorName` or the corresponding build command's `--flavor` option.
Read the active flavor with Flutter's `appFlavor` value and choose that environment's endpoint or other configured values.
For iOS, select the corresponding configured Xcode scheme through the Flutter command's `--flavor` option.

briefs.learning_objective: Produce one release Android bundle authenticated by the supplied upload-signing configuration.

required_facts.statement: Configure release signing with the upload keystore, key alias, and passwords referenced by private keystore properties.
Load those properties in Gradle and assign the release signing configuration rather than use the debug key for a distributable release.
Keep keystore material and key.properties private and out of public source control.
Run `flutter build appbundle` with the intended environment and release configuration to create the Android App Bundle.
The release bundle is written under `build/app/outputs/bundle/release/` for the standard non-flavored release configuration.

briefs.learning_objective: Produce one iOS distribution artifact matching supplied signing and provisioning access.

required_facts.statement: For iOS, select the registered Apple developer team and configure Xcode Signing & Capabilities so the bundle's signing and provisioning match its application identity.
Run `flutter build ipa` on the configured macOS/Xcode environment to create the iOS archive and IPA for distribution.
The command outputs an xcarchive under `build/ios/archive/` and the IPA under `build/ios/ipa/`.
Open the archive in Xcode, use Validate App, correct reported problems, and distribute the validated build to App Store Connect.

briefs.learning_objective: Prepare one supplied listing so its required metadata and assets satisfy the store checklist.

required_facts.statement: Keep descriptions, screenshots, previews, and privacy information accurate to the submitted application's actual behavior.
Complete the store listing and app-content information required by Play Console before submitting its release.
Declare requested sensitive permissions and applicable app content accurately rather than omit functionality present in the build.
Prepare the store's required listing text and graphic assets in its prescribed languages, counts, dimensions, and formats; check those properties against the current store listing specification.

briefs.learning_objective: Complete one supplied disclosure checklist so it matches actual app data and permission behavior.

required_facts.statement: Publish an accessible privacy policy describing collected data, its uses, third-party sharing, retention, deletion, and consent withdrawal.
Inventory data collected or shared by the application and its third-party SDKs rather than report only collection written directly in application code.
Map that actual inventory to the Google Play Data safety declarations, including the relevant collection, sharing, security, and deletion information.
Check privacy declarations against the shipped permission and telemetry behavior and update them when the implementation changes.

briefs.learning_objective: Verify one release main flow and supplied reviewer access and identify any blocking failure.

required_facts.statement: Review the release as an actual user-facing application and resolve crashes, bugs, broken links, and incomplete behavior before submission.
Test its release build on the intended supported targets and verify that backend services required by the journey are live and accessible.
Provide working review access, such as a demo account or supported demo mode, for account-gated functionality.
On Google Play, resolve errors reported in the release review summary before publishing; warnings should also be addressed where possible.

briefs.learning_objective: Follow one supplied submission workflow and identify its next valid step and review state.

required_facts.statement: Complete the release's required build, listing, app-content declarations, and release notes, then resolve blocking errors in the store review summary before submitting.
Google Play Changes not yet sent for review means changes exist but have not been submitted; send those changes for review through Publishing overview rather than assume upload submitted them.
In review means the store is reviewing the update, not that it has already been published.
For App rejected or Update rejected, read the policy issue, correct it and resubmit, or use the supported appeal process.
Choose the intended testing or production audience and verify the published status and availability; publication timing can be controlled through managed publishing on Google Play.
Uploading an iOS build to App Store Connect first starts build processing; wait for processing to finish before selecting the build for its version and submission workflow.
